metadata.title: Title Search Explained: The Hidden Liens Investors Miss
metadata.author: Logan Fullmer
metadata.shortDescription:
A county records search only catches about 75% of the problems on a property. The other 25% are unrecorded municipal liens: water bills, code violations, and other debts tracked at the city or township level. Alex Goldovsky, founder of ProTitle USA, has spent 19 years finding what title reports miss, for everyone from small investors to Wall Street firms and Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

Alex started ProTitle during the 2008 financial crisis after a call from the FDIC, which needed help as it closed failed banks. Today his company handles a large share of title and tax reports on wholesale capital-market transactions, with human searchers on the ground in counties that still don't have online records.

In this episode of Dirty Deeds, Alex Goldovsky and Logan Fullmer break down how a title report can reveal your negotiating discount, which liens survive a foreclosure and which get wiped out, why a million-dollar IRS lien can sometimes be released for about $10,000, and how his curative team clears old unreleased mortgages. They also cover note investing, replacement title policies, and a DSCR loan fraud ring that bought more than 250 properties in Baltimore.

You'll learn:
- Why "more hair" on a title report can mean a bigger discount
- Which liens survive a foreclosure, and when an HOA can wipe out a first
- How IRS liens can sometimes be negotiated for pennies
- What unrecorded municipal liens are, and how to find them
- Why human searchers still beat AI for title research
- How to clear an old unreleased mortgage
- What a replacement title policy is and when note buyers need one
- How appraisal and deed fraud schemes work, and what to watch for
